loot_editor.help.root: Each pool runs when the chest first generates loot, including hopper access. After generation it is a normal shared inventory.
loot_editor.help.pools: Pools execute independently, with their own rolls, entries, conditions and functions.
loot_editor.help.entries: Each roll selects eligible weighted entries: items, empty rewards, tags, referenced tables or composites.
loot_editor.help.rolls: How many times this pool selects candidates. Use a fixed number or an advanced random range. Rolls is not the final item count.
loot_editor.help.bonus_rolls: Extra rolls derived from player luck, added to rolls using native rounding rules.
loot_editor.help.weight: Relative weight, not a percentage. With only weights 1 and 3 and identical conditions, the chances are 25% and 75%.
loot_editor.help.quality: Luck contribution to effective weight; this is not equipment quality or enchantment level.
loot_editor.help.conditions: Controls whether the enclosing pool, entry or function runs. Placement determines its scope.
loot_editor.help.functions: Processing applied to selected items, such as count, enchantments or name. Preserve unfamiliar processing rules.
loot_editor.help.type: Namespaced type identifier. Container root: minecraft:chest; common entries: minecraft:item, minecraft:tag, minecraft:loot_table.
loot_editor.help.name: Resource identifier of the item, tag or referenced loot table. Preserve referenced dependencies when exporting.
loot_editor.help.count: Count provider for this item entry. Other functions may modify the final count.
loot_editor.help.children: Nested entries. alternatives, sequence and group have different execution rules; they are not interchangeable weighted pools.
loot_editor.help.expand: Whether a tag expands its items into separate candidates; this affects selection weights.
loot_editor.help.random_sequence: Optional native random sequence identifier. This is not a fixed reward list.
loot_editor.help.generic: An original rule node. Open its children to inspect it; unknown mod fields are preserved. Open the advanced help for nesting and value syntax.
loot_editor.workflow: 1. Select/add a pool; 2. Add/update items; 3. Save and apply; 4. Assign to the selected container.

loot_editor.guide.basics.1: A loot table defines how items are generated. It is not a chest that already contains those items.
loot_editor.guide.basics.2: A resource ID uniquely names a table, such as hhu_author:chests/camp. The namespace is before the colon; the path is after it.
loot_editor.guide.basics.3: Pools run independently when their conditions pass. Separate pools can provide food and equipment.
loot_editor.guide.basics.4: Rolls specifies how many times a pool runs. A normal roll selects a candidate, and repeated rolls can select the same item.
loot_editor.guide.basics.5: Entries are candidates: items, empty results, referenced tables or composite rules. Basic editing focuses on ordinary item entries.
loot_editor.guide.basics.6: Start by creating or copying a table, adding a pool, setting rolls, adding items with weights and counts, saving, then binding an empty test container.
loot_editor.guide.chance.1: Weight is relative to other eligible candidates in the same pool, not a percentage. Increasing a sole candidate weight does not increase its output.
loot_editor.guide.chance.2: For one roll with bread weight 3 and iron weight 1, chances are 75% and 25% if there are no extra conditions, luck modifiers or special entries.
loot_editor.guide.chance.3: Count controls how many items one selection produces. Multiple rolls instead make separate selections and can select different candidates.
loot_editor.guide.chance.4: An empty entry participates in weighted selection but generates nothing when selected.
loot_editor.guide.chance.5: Conditions gate pools or entries, such as a random chance or an entity requirement. Required context varies; a failed condition can produce nothing.
loot_editor.guide.chance.6: Quality changes effective weight using luck; bonus_rolls can add rolls. Neither guarantees rare loot or necessarily affects ordinary chest generation.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.1: Advanced editing shows nested rules. $ means the entire table. Open a row to enter it and use Up to return. Bracketed English names retain the original keys.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.2: An object {…} contains named settings; a list […] contains ordered elements. List indexes 0, 1, 2 are positions, not counts or chances.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.3: $ → pools → 0 → entries → 0 is the first entry of the first pool. Pool rolls changes selections; item weight changes relative chance.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.4: Type identifies a rule kind; an item name identifies its item ID. Functions process selected items, including set_count and set_nbt.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.5: Write numbers without quotes, text in double quotes, and switches as true or false. Editing changes the draft until you publish it.
loot_editor.guide.advanced.6: Appending to an object requires a field name and value; a list needs only a value. Deleting removes the selected node and its children. Preserve unfamiliar mod fields and experiment on copies.
loot_editor.guide.examples.1: Guaranteed food: one pool, one roll, one bread entry with count 3–3 produces three bread if no other conditions apply.
loot_editor.guide.examples.2: Bread and carrots with equal weights and two rolls can select either twice. This does not guarantee one of each.
loot_editor.guide.examples.3: Use separate pools for guaranteed food and optional equipment. In the equipment pool, weighted equipment and empty entries control its chance.
loot_editor.guide.examples.4: Basic count settings usually appear as minecraft:set_count in functions. Existing enchantment or naming functions may also modify output.
loot_editor.guide.examples.5: Alternatives uses the first passing child; sequence runs children until failure; group combines children. These are not all ordinary mutually exclusive weighted pools.
loot_editor.guide.examples.6: Test with a new empty container. A chest whose loot has already generated does not reroll merely by reopening it.
loot_editor.guide.containers.1: Binding assigns a table for later generation, not immediate item transfer. Loot usually generates on first access, which some mods may trigger early.
loot_editor.guide.containers.2: Publish and bind are separate: save and activate the table before assigning it. An unsaved draft cannot be bound as an active table.
loot_editor.guide.containers.3: Existing contents are protected unless replacement is explicitly confirmed. Confirm you no longer need those items before replacing them.
loot_editor.guide.containers.4: A double chest has two block entities. Check the displayed half count; each half may generate its own loot rather than sharing one roll.
loot_editor.guide.containers.5: Barrels, shulker boxes and mod containers require a supported loot interface. An unsupported message does not mean the block cannot store items.
loot_editor.guide.containers.6: Bind containers before capturing a structure, and avoid opening them first. Captured container data may contain fixed items if loot already generated.
loot_editor.guide.files.1: The library reads the server loaded loot tables from vanilla, mods and data packs. Namespace prefixes distinguish their sources.
loot_editor.guide.files.2: Other mods tables are readable but their original files are not overwritten. Copy into hhu_author before editing your own version.
loot_editor.guide.files.3: Save and apply submits the draft for server validation. Confirm success and active status before binding; local changes alone are not a published table.
loot_editor.guide.files.4: Export creates files for packaging. Moving a structure to another server also requires transferring any custom tables it references.
loot_editor.guide.files.5: External files are managed by the server, not each client. After manual file edits, use external reload and confirm the result.
loot_editor.guide.files.6: Data packs can override an ID; the final server loaded version wins. Unknown mod fields are retained but not all can be explained here; test in game.
loot_editor.help.pool: This is one pool. Open rolls to change selections, or entries to inspect its candidates.
loot_editor.help.entry: This is one candidate. Type identifies its kind, name identifies its content, weight changes relative chance, and functions process its output.
loot_editor.help.function: This ID chooses an item processing function, such as minecraft:set_count. Fill its other parameters according to that function.
loot_editor.help.condition: This ID chooses a test, such as minecraft:random_chance. Its other parameters depend on the selected condition.
loot_editor.cache_restored: Local world draft restored; reload or publish before binding.
loot_editor.cache_cleared: Draft cleared. Published loot tables are unchanged.

developer_guide.title: Developer tool catalog
developer_guide.intro: Select a tool for instructions. This guide grants no privileges; authoring normally requires creative mode or operator permissions.
developer_guide.hover: See Developer tool catalog for detailed instructions.
developer_guide.creative_soldier_control: Right-click an unowned human to configure guard, pursuit and patrol behavior for building templates. This does not hire it. Keep patrol points inside the white capture bounds; placement transforms their relative positions.
developer_guide.patrol_command_baton.det: Select a human you may command, then record world waypoints as prompted. Review waypoints and wait settings with their outlines. Template routes must stay within capture bounds.
developer_guide.natural_state_tool.summa: Manage natural identity and site behavior
developer_guide.natural_state_tool.detai: Inspect and configure natural identity and spawn behavior. This is not a hiring contract; use the creative controller to review current commands.
developer_guide.attribute_observer.detai: Right-click a human to inspect server-provided health, specialties and attribute sources. Useful for faction, tier and growth comparisons; reading does not reroll attributes.
Select humans and a destination as prompted. Cycle the diagnostic focus or clear selections using the tool controls. Fixed-point tests temporarily own movement; autonomous behavior resumes after testing.
developer_guide.navigation_observer_helm: View marked humans' paths, vision, sound clues and decisions. F8 opens global budgets; entity details show action ownership. A diagnostic mark does not necessarily mean a confirmed target.
developer_guide.human_monitor.summary: Monitor and take over a human
developer_guide.human_monitor.detail: Bind a human by right-clicking it, then use away from entities to monitor. Controls display the current key bindings. Survival access is limited to your hired soldiers; creative mode can test other humans.
developer_guide.wild_human_cleanup.detai: Clean up unhired humans in test scenes; hired soldiers are excluded. Check permission and scope before use to avoid removing template inhabitants you still need.
developer_guide.settlement_information.d: Choose building, settlement or broker-station type and a template name, then capture white bounds with the selector. Regions, facilities and inhabitants are saved with the template. Ordinary huts do not require courtyard regions.
developer_guide.settlement_region_tool.d: Sneak-click the information block to bind, then sneak-use to open the selector. Choose a region type and two corners, then confirm. Left-click cancels the current selection. The panel lists regions, removal controls and persistent visibility.
developer_guide.settlement_facility_tool: Register facility blocks to a building

Bind the information block, then right-click a facility. Create eligible regions first: task boards belong to an outer courtyard outside inner regions; follow the placement hints for other facilities. Placing a block alone does not register it.
developer_guide.settlement_selection_too: Sneak-use to choose a saved server template. Right-click the world to preview, then right-click to adjust position, rotation and mirroring. Leaving the panel retains the preview; confirm to place, or left-click to cancel.
developer_guide.loot_editor.detail: Use on a container to configure its table, or in air to browse tables. Copy vanilla or mod tables before editing. Publish your draft, then explicitly bind it. Loot rolls on the first container opening. The Help tab explains rules; local drafts are cached automatically.
navigation_debug.detail.monitor_hint: Monitor: current target only, no helmet or pointer needed. Previous selections resume on exit.
navigation_debug.detail.spectator_hint: Spectator: only pointer-marked humans are displayed. Layer switches apply; previous selections resume on exit.
navigation_debug.detail.capacity_hint: Some details were truncated for network limits. Observed entities, focus and action ownership are retained.
navigation_debug.detail.unbound_hint: Unbound: native GoalSelector state only; movement ownership is not coordinated.
navigation_debug.detail.action_truncated: Actions, goals, progress and feedback were truncated to protocol limits.
